data_stores.ask: Where is data stored, and which part of the system owns each store?
data_stores.why: Each store needs one owner so data stays consistent.

data_flows.ask: How does data move between stores and systems: copies, syncs, exports, events?

schema_changes.ask: How will changes to stored data be rolled out without breaking the running system?
schema_changes.explain: A migration is a controlled change to the structure or content of stored data.

backup_restore.ask: How is data backed up, and how quickly must it be restorable?

retention.ask: How long is each kind of data kept, and are there legal or contractual rules about deleting it or where it lives?

api_consumers.ask: Who calls the API or uses its events: your own apps, other teams, outside partners? Do they release on their own schedule?
api_consumers.why: Consumers who release separately need compatibility promises, and maybe a written contract.

failure_tolerance.ask: When a dependency is slow or down, should requests wait, retry, fail fast or degrade?

hosting_responsibility.ask: Is the backend hosted and run by your team, or is it a managed service you only configure?
hosting_responsibility.why: A managed service used as-is needs much less operational design than services you run yourself.

docs/backend-api/DATA.md.purpose: Data architecture when it needs its own document: stores, flows, migrations, backup, retention and residency.
docs/backend-api/DATA.md.skip: Created only when there are several data stores, live migrations, or backup, retention or residency rules.
